newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at an intraday high of 8.2951 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2959 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to speculative buying in the last few minutes of trading, traders said.
China's heavy foreign trade surplus in the first three months of this year added dollar supply to the market, helping push up the yuan today, they said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2961.
The yuan opened up at 8.2955 and moved between 8.2955 and 8.2959 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2960 late in trading before the speculative buying pushed it back up again.
Trading was active with most business done at about 8.2958, traders said.
One dealer said the size of China's foreign trade surplus in the first quarter continued to be a factor supporting the yuan.
"The speculative buying in the last few minutes was unexpected, but the yuan's movement overall proves it is still strong partly thanks to the foreign trade surplus," he said.
China on Monday reported a trade surplus of $6.71 billion in the first three months of this year, up 25.7 percent year-on-year.
A second dealer said the yuan's rise showed signs of faltering on Wednesday as it approached the 8.2950 resistance level.
"The market expects the central bank to intervene if the yuan breaches that level," he said. "This has made it a strong psychological barrier for the yuan."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to consolidate on Thursday after rises over the past three days.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.5610 from 6.5695 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0714 against the Hong Kong dollar. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
